questions.q: What function does customers.sql use to reference the staging model, and how does that differ from source()?
options: source() — ref() is only used for raw tables, never for models
ref() — it points at a model this project already built, while source() points at raw data this project didn't build
There's no difference; ref() and source() are interchangeable
import() — a function unique to the marts layer
questions.explain: ref('stg_jaffle_shop__customers') points at the staging model built in Lesson 6, which is the defining difference from source(), which points at raw, un-modeled data.

questions.q: Why is this project's customers.sql almost identical to the staging model it builds on, rather than adding joins or business logic?
options: The staging model already contains all possible business logic
This Beginner project only has one source table, so there's nothing yet to join and no derived business logic to compute, given the scope drawn in Lesson 1
dbt doesn't allow joins inside mart models
Mart models are required by dbt to be exact copies of their staging model
questions.explain: The mart layer is where joins and business logic belong in bigger projects, but this project's deliberately narrow scope (Lesson 1) means there's nothing yet to add — the Intermediate capstone is where that changes.

questions.q: What's the real value of having a separate customers mart model, even though it looks so similar to staging here?
options: customers is the name a stakeholder would expect to query — marts are the layer meant to be seen, unlike internal staging models
It runs faster than querying the staging model directly
It's required because Snowflake doesn't allow querying staging-named tables
It automatically adds order and payment data
questions.explain: Even when the transformation is minimal, the mart layer gives stakeholders a stable, expected table name to query, separate from internal staging-model naming.

questions.q: What happens if you run `dbt run --select customers` before stg_jaffle_shop__customers has ever been built?
options: dbt automatically builds the staging model first, because customers.sql references it with ref()
The run fails immediately with no explanation
dbt builds an empty customers table with no columns
dbt silently skips the customers model
questions.explain: Because ref() creates a dependency edge dbt understands, dbt's dependency-aware build order builds the referenced staging model first automatically.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what would make the customers mart start looking meaningfully different from the staging model?
options: Switching from Snowflake to a different warehouse
Running dbt test instead of dbt run
Joining in order history, as the Intermediate capstone does next in this series
Renaming the customer_id column again
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly points to the Intermediate capstone, which joins in order history, as where this mart's scope — and its divergence from staging — grows.
